newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar closes steady but quiet.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar closes steady but quiet.

text.p: White sugar futures held within the narrow trading ranges set earlier in the day and the low level of activity showed no signs of livening-up.
Near March last traded at $311.60, down $0.30 a tonne from Friday, and other positions closed between $0.10 a tonne lower and $0.40 higher. Turnover totalled 619 lots.

Physical news was thin on the ground, although traders cited talk that Iraq had concluded a deal to buy between four and six cargoes of refined white sugar under the U.N. oil-for-food deal. The origin was likely to be European, they said, but added that details of price were as yet unclear.
The terms of Iraq's original tender specify either Brazil or France but also a range of qualities between the European 45 ICUMSA standard and lesser-quality 100 ICUMSA.
Paris white sugar ended $0.20 lower to $1.00 a tonne higher with March last trading at $311.10.
